detailed_description:
The target video is a 15-second dark-pop / cyber-grunge rap music video in a late-1990s to early-2000s independent-magazine zine collage aesthetic: high-contrast black and white with low-saturation dark-red and silver-grey accents, true-to-life skin tones, heavy blacks that still preserve clothing detail; coarse film grain, halftone dots, print ragged edges, and plate misregistration run through the whole video; only hard cuts, jump cuts, flash-to-white cuts, flash-to-black cuts, and beat-matched cuts are used, with no dissolves or soft transitions, no neon-soaked cyberpunk or game-CG gloss; the members' performance is locked to the drums like a real rap performance, never a runway walk or a static pose.
[Shot 1] A pure-black frame hard-cuts on a bass hit into an extreme close-up of <Subject 1>, 24mm wide-angle close to her face as she leans toward the lens and snaps her head downward on the beat, her long straight black hair swinging slightly; the background is overexposed white, a huge bold black "NO" sits behind her head with its middle hidden by her head; film grain surges and the frame jolts slightly up and down.
[Shot 2] At 00:00.800, a hard cut to a close-up of <Subject 2>'s shoulder and jaw: she lowers her shoulders and glances sideways into the lens, then snaps her face square to camera on the snare, long wavy black hair sweeping across her eye corner without covering her eyes; halftone dots bleed from the background into the beaded edges of her corset top; condensed "SIGNAL" is hard-cut compressed in from the right, between the background and her foreground shoulder.
[Shot 3] At 00:01.500, a hard cut to a low-angle medium shot of <Subject 3>: she thrusts one hand toward the lens, the palm sweeping across the foreground, pulling back on a bass hit as her body presses forward, her bright red hair and slipping red jacket moving with real inertia; the red and black plates misregister slightly like an old magazine scan; "BITE" is partially covered by her hand.
[Shot 4] At 00:02.300, a hard cut to a tight frontal medium shot of all three, standing close: <Subject 1> center, <Subject 2> and <Subject 3> flanking her; together they press their shoulders down, then lift their heads to stare into the lens on the beat; the background hard-cuts from white to black and back to white; large "BREAK" stretches horizontally behind them, their bodies masking its middle.
[Shot 5] At 00:03.000, a hard cut to a 50mm side close-up of <Subject 1>: she turns, stops abruptly, her face rotating from profile toward the lens as a ringed finger rakes quickly along her jawline; the camera pushes in half a step exactly on the stop point; "CTRL" sits in the left foreground, slightly overlapping her leather-jacket shoulder but not her face.
[Shot 6] At 00:03.700, a hard cut to a low-angle full shot of <Subject 2>: a short, real dance move - knees knocking inward, torso pulling back, arms slicing across her chest, then immediately lunging toward the lens; her sheer embellished skirt and corset straps snap with clear dynamics; on the snare the frame flips to black-and-white halftone for three frames, then back to color.
[Shot 7] At 00:04.400, a hard cut to a 35mm tight face shot of <Subject 3>: she lifts her chin slightly on the rhythm, then leans in, a defiant real rap expression rather than a smile; dark-red "LOST" cuts suddenly from behind her into the foreground, pressing over her red hair and jacket without covering her eyes.
[Shot 8] At 00:05.100, a rapid montage of alternating head nods: <Subject 1> nodding frontally, <Subject 2> whipping her wavy hair from the side, <Subject 3> pressing her head forward - each action held only three to five frames across three consecutive hard cuts; the background flips between white, grey, and black as film scan lines roll briefly up and down.
[Shot 9] At 00:06.000, a hard cut to a two-shot of <Subject 1> and <Subject 3>: <Subject 1> raps straight into the lens while <Subject 3> suddenly pops out from behind her toward the camera, the foreground-background layering kept clear; "ZERO" sits in the background and "MERCY" low in the foreground, pressing over costume but not faces.
[Shot 10] At 00:06.800, a hard cut to a medium-close single of <Subject 2>: her hands cross quickly beside her face then slice outward on consecutive snares; the camera whip-pans left in sync and locks dead on the final accent; torn photocopy paper and black tape graphics appear glued on the studio wall behind her.
[Shot 11] At 00:07.600, a hard cut to a full-shot wide of all three: they are not dancing in unison but in echoing moves - <Subject 1> stepping forward with shoulders pressing down, <Subject 2> folding sideways with her skirt flaring, <Subject 3> turning away then snapping back toward the lens - every move freezing together on the same bass hit.
[Shot 12] At 00:08.500, an extreme-close hand montage: <Subject 1>'s silver rings, a waist chain, a jacket zipper, fingers tapping a thigh, a palm pushing toward the lens, each detail held only two to four frames; torn-paper letter fragments "BR / EA / K" hard-cut and reassemble across frame positions like clipped letters.
[Shot 13] At 00:09.300, a hard cut to <Subject 3> rapping in the foreground, 24mm very close: one finger points at the lens, then the wrist twists and presses downward; <Subject 2> and <Subject 1> stay blurred behind her, still making small head and shoulder movements; the frame builds three layers - background "FRAME", mid-ground two members, foreground <Subject 3> and her gesture.
[Shot 14] At 00:10.200, <Subject 2> sweeps in fast from frame left: her wavy hair and sheer skirt swing through the turn, then her face lands close beside the lens, eyes locked on camera; on the accent a slight horizontal scan displacement hits, a red-cyan plate shift tracing her outline while her skin tone stays natural.
[Shot 15] At 00:11.100, a hard cut to <Subject 1> in a frontal center medium shot: she drops her gaze for half a beat, then snaps her head up as <Subject 2> and <Subject 3> press forward from behind her at the same moment and the camera pulls back a fast step for real spatial impact; giant "BITE BACK" cuts suddenly from the background into the space between foreground and the members, sliced into pieces by their bodies.
[Shot 16] At 00:12.000, three consecutive hard cuts, each on a snare: <Subject 1>'s ringed fingers pushing at the lens, <Subject 2>'s shoulder driving toward camera, <Subject 3> turning back over her shoulder; grain and print noise thicken with each cut.
[Shot 17] At 00:13.000, a hard cut to a low-angle heroic full shot of all three: <Subject 1> one step forward at center, <Subject 2> crouching her weight low at her side, <Subject 3> leaning her torso forward; all three keep real breathing and micro-sway, never a frozen pose; the background text "NO SIGNAL" is partially blocked by the members, only split letterforms visible.
[Shot 18] At 00:14.000, on the final bass hit: the camera plunges into a close three-face shot as all three nod once and stare into the lens; the frame slams into a high-contrast black-and-white photocopy look; the original text "ECLIPSE MODE" appears briefly between their backs and foreground shoulders, vibrating twice; a final hard cut to pure black - no fade.

overall_soundscape: A faint dead-studio room tone underlies the whole video; hair whips, fabric swishes, and hand movements carry small realistic friction sounds, and every cut lands tight against the music's transients.

non_diegetic_music: A 138 BPM dark-pop / cyber-grunge / trap-rap track drives the entire video: heavy sub-bass, dry cracking snares, distorted electronic noise, and short rap vocal chops; the first three seconds build pressure, the middle section runs a continuous rap flow, and the final two seconds close on a heavy bass hit.
